newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch firms say two years to recover Euro-costs.
newsitem.headline: Dutch firms say two years to recover Euro-costs.

text.p: Dutch companies believe they will need just over two years on average to recover the costs related to the introduction of a single European currency, according to a poll conducted by the Dutch central bank.
But the bank said in its quarterly report Dutch companies also expected to reap annual advantages of some 6.6 billion guilders -- one percent of GDP -- from the euro's introduction in the long term.
One-off costs for training, administration, software and treasury activities to prepare for the new currency were expected to total some 6-7 billion guilders.

The Dutch central bank said the poll indicated Dutch companies saw euro-related costs mounting to about 5.5 billion guilders. Banks have already set aside provisions totalling some one billion guilders.
"This means that the total business community will spend 6 to 7 billion guilders in the move to a single (European) currency," the Dutch central bank said.
Of the total expected annual savings of some 6.6 billion guilders, business expected 2.3 billion guilders to occur immediately after the euro's introduction.
Immediate savings would come from the elimination of costs to cover currency risk and simplified book keeping.
The central bank said the manufacturing industry would likely recoup its costs faster than food retailers.
According to the poll, manufacturing sector companies estimated they would break even in six months to two years, wholesalers in six months to a year and food retailers in two to four years.
Retailers in other sectors would require three-and-a-half years to break even, and private sector consultancies and services around one to three years, the poll showed.
